feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain depth in public-sector, Drupal, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally and shows progression well, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility through specifics: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Broad yet coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/web delivery, analytics, AI search, and multimedia all align well with the target brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy/operations/workflows/governance” appears often across sections; consolidate Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT to avoid overlap.  
- Add more outcome-focused impact: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; punctuation/hyphenation varies (“organization-wide” vs. “cross-department,” “AI-enabled” usage, bullet formatting in content blocks). “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler and can be removed.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s seniority and public-sector focus. It would be more impactful with a clearer value proposition, a few concrete signals of scale, and slightly less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground scope/scale: “Senior digital and communications leader with 12+ years leading enterprise web modernization and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add 1–2 concrete proof points from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace the generic “Leads…” sentence with outcome-oriented language: “Builds governance, analytics, and editorial systems that improve publishing efficiency, audience discovery, and cross-channel coordination.”
- Consider trimming “multimedia production” or “AI-enabled user experiences” unless you want those as differentiators in the intro; they’re already well covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models,” “content operations,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…” repeat heavily across Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Platforms” is vague; specify web/CMS platforms if kept.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less overlapping capability areas with sharper wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and reduce repetition with other sections:
  Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial systems & publishing operations • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow automation, integrations & platform delivery • AI-enabled search & content discovery • Public-sector advocacy & multi-channel communications • Multimedia, livestream & studio operations
- Change “communications operations” to “communications” or “communications leadership” for a stronger executive tone.
- Consider replacing “platform integration” with “integrations” for cleaner parallel structure.
- Keep phrasing noun-based and consistent; all items should read as capability areas, not mixed functions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics,” “AI-enabled search,” and “multimedia production” are already emphasized in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills: “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block overlaps heavily with Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more uniform will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence with strong verbs.
- Standardize style: use serial commas, hyphenate consistently (“bill-level,” “AI-enabled”), and spell out “10 x 20-foot” for cleaner formatting.
- Emphasize outcomes or scope where possible: e.g., “to improve policy-content discovery” or “built for ongoing campaign expansion.”
- Consider this tighter rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Developed a multi-part digital campaign spanning editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Launched a recurring advocacy video program covering planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent roles.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most unique value because it introduces experiential/display work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the footer projects and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the consulting value you personally delivered.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and foreground impact: combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on improving coordination, publishing efficiency, or decision-making.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, toolkits launched, teams enabled, publishing time reduced, search success/engagement improvements.
- Use stronger action/result phrasing, e.g. “Built Drupal microsites and modular campaign components that enabled reusable storytelling, downloadable member resources, and faster campaign launches.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet higher-level here.
- Drupal microsites/toolkits/storytelling also overlaps with “We Are Counties Microsite”; avoid repeating the same implementation details.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with an impact-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets, led by the website modernization: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcome language where possible: improved publishing speed, reporting adoption, campaign capacity, production cost/time savings, or engagement growth from the studio/analytics work.
- Tighten phrasing: “Expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to standardize reporting and improve decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; either add distinct results here or cut it.
- Video-program expansion also appears in earlier NACo roles; keep this item focused on building the in-house studio and scaling capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel ownership, and systems you scaled before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging prior to promotion to Director of Digital Media.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add stronger action/result framing: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Clarify operational impact: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes and standardized digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director role’s opening line.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry and footer project; keep only if framed as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong theme fit, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the leadership/value angle and use tighter phrasing that complements, rather than repeats, the experience section.

Suggested edit
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented skill labels:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for high-volume publishing
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Tighten “Editorial systems and governance” to “Editorial operations for high-volume publishing” if you want clearer alignment with the 10,000+ page / 50+ publisher experience.
- If space allows, add one scale cue in the section intro elsewhere, not here, to avoid turning skills into mini-bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat the header/Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” and several NACo bullets unless made more specific.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize recent strengths tied to current/most recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Lead with Drupal and CMS modernization since those are most supported by recent roles; de-emphasize older or less-evidenced platforms if space is tight.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority platform to improve focus: keep “WordPress” only if actively relevant to target roles.
- Use “search and discovery” instead of “search experiences” for a sharper, more enterprise-ready phrase.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and avoid repeating every platform.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies almost verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads more like a tool dump than a senior capability statement. Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic phrases with stronger senior wording: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting”
- Add one optimization concept if accurate: “SEO, UX and performance analysis” or “dashboarding and insight generation”

Possible rewrite:
- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- KPI framework development and executive reporting
- SEO, UX and performance analysis

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Avoid listing the same tools in both places unless this version is clearly more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it tighter, more senior, and oriented to operational scope rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Studio, Video & Hybrid Event Production”
- Replace with concise, higher-level terms: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Virtual event technical direction • End-to-end production workflows”
- If space allows, add one stronger capability instead of “editing,” e.g. “Run of show and technical troubleshooting” or “Remote guest and signal management”
- Keep wording consistent with seniority; avoid entry-level phrasing like “video editing” unless paired with leadership/operations language

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially duplicates Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); consider keeping detail here and shortening/removing that phrase there.
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the NACo role bullet about building an in-house studio; don’t repeat that accomplishment in skills.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills almost exactly. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/current platforms or expanded slightly to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current, high-value platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add brief qualifiers for differentiation, not just a tool list: e.g., “Drupal (10, enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use “CMS & Web Platforms” if you want a slightly stronger heading.
- If GitHub Pages was only light use, consider dropping it to keep the list focused on enterprise-relevant platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly redundant with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- Avoid repeating platform names elsewhere unless this section adds specificity or proficiency context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add specificity where credible: “API integrations and tag implementation (Google Tag Manager)”
- Group modern tooling together: “Edge/serverless scripting: Cloudflare Workers”
- Clarify delivery workflow: “Version control and deployment automation: GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; either remove them there or make this section the detailed version.
- If Cloudflare Workers or GitHub Actions were only lightly used, consider dropping one to avoid overstating hands-on engineering depth.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools”
- Group by function to show judgment, not just inventory: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If accurate, add a light qualifier for impact: “Used to build editorial planning systems, cross-team workflows, and lightweight automations”
- Consider dropping the weakest/oldest-use tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most relevant to recent work (Airtable, Power Automate, Jira/Asana, Slack/Teams)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; listing both is fine, but they add less value than automation platforms unless tied to workflow use.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or use case. It should read as a concise platform list, not repeat the email leadership already covered in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS matching: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use without turning this into a duplicate achievement line: enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, member engagement
- Example rewrite: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise email campaigns • Newsletter and member engagement operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding audience size, newsletter volume, or channel leadership here; those are already stronger in the NACo experience entries.
- Don’t repeat “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and work history.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo Director role. Use it to sharpen technical specificity rather than repeat broad capability claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Data & Analytics Tools
- Tighten content to: GA4 • Google Tag Manager • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity
- Move broad methods out of this line: replace “SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding” with either more concrete tools or drop them entirely
- If you want to keep optimization language, use: Analytics implementation • KPI reporting • UX behavior analysis (better as a separate skills line than mixed with tools)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” almost exactly; consider keeping detail in one place only.
- “Dashboarding” is already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI, so it adds little value.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content ownership, and any concrete outputs or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Add clearer scope and actions: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; improved publishing workflows; contributed to a major website refresh.”
- Tighten the content-production line: “Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates to expand NACo’s digital advocacy and member communications.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos, audience growth, email/social reach, website traffic, or team size/mentorship scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital/media growth, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program support and the first-podcast launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through production.”
- Tighten supporting detail: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including planning, scripting and episode production for a new audio program.”
- If possible, add scope or adoption metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a two-part structure: one clause on research/program coordination, one on digital/media execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” language already covered more strongly in later digital media roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/editorial operations here; those are better established in 2015–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already established in recent roles. Tightening it to tools plus production capabilities will make it cleaner and more credible.

Suggested edit
